reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms boron-induced (Hf, Zr)B2 precipitation at grain boundaries in a bulk HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy and shows enhanced grain-boundary cohesion, but it does not address nanoparticle synthesis, diffusion-barrier function, or suppression of sintering/phase segregation under catalytic or thermoelectric conditions. The key mechanistic premises about diffusion barriers and high-temperature stability are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Boron segregates to grain boundaries in refractory HEA nanoparticles
Boron forms stable (Hf, Zr)B2 precipitates at grain boundaries
Intergranular borides act as diffusion barriers that suppress atomic mobility
Suppressed atomic mobility inhibits sintering and phase segregation at high temperature
The effect is achievable with ~0.1 at.% boron doping in nanoparticles
